blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Block Fence Cost in Cheltenham in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out what Cheltenham homeowners can expect to pay for a new core-filled block fence, including materials, labour, and council considerations.
body: If you are a Cheltenham homeowner considering a new block fence, understanding the true cost upfront will help you budget with confidence and avoid costly surprises. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we price block fencing based on wall height, length, block type, foundation requirements, and site accessibility. A standard two-metre high core-filled block fence in Cheltenham typically starts from around $120 to $180 per square metre, depending on the complexity of the job and the finish you require. Factors like access to your side boundary, the type of footing required, and whether capping or rendering is included will all influence the final price.

One of the most common questions we hear from Cheltenham clients is whether hollow block walls are cheaper than core-filled options. The answer is yes — hollow block walls use less concrete and are generally more affordable. However, for front fences and boundary walls that need to withstand Melbourne's unpredictable weather, core-filled blocks provide vastly superior strength, wind resistance, and longevity. For a typical Cheltenham front fence measuring eight metres long by two metres high, a core-filled block wall will likely cost between $2,000 and $3,200, including materials, labour, and footings.

Cheltenham sits within the City of Kingston, which has specific requirements regarding fence height, setbacks, and planning permits. Generally, a fence under two metres does not require a planning permit in Victoria, but you must check with your neighbours and ensure the fence complies with theSPATH Fences Act 1968. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we help our Cheltenham clients navigate these requirements and can advise on any council considerations before we begin. Getting this right from the start prevents disputes and costly rework down the line.

Another important cost factor is the foundation. Cheltenham's soil varies across different pockets, and many properties in the area have reactive clay soils that require engineered footings. Skipping or undersizing footings is one of the biggest mistakes we see in block fencing across Melbourne's south-east. A proper footing for a two-metre block fence in Cheltenham will typically be 450mm wide by 600mm deep, reinforced with steel, and poured on a compacted gravel base. This adds to the upfront cost but protects your investment for decades.

The finish of your block fence also affects the overall cost. A basic block wall with capping on top is the most affordable option. If you want the wall rendered, parged, or painted, expect to add $40 to $80 per square metre. Many Cheltenham homeowners opt for a smooth or textured render finish because it dramatically improves the look of the fence and adds a layer of weather protection to the blockwork. Mega Brick & Blocks can help you choose the right finish for your property and budget.

At the end of the day, the best way to get an accurate cost for your Cheltenham block fence is to have a professional builder inspect your site. Every property is different — access, soil conditions, existing structures, and boundary positions all play a role. Mega Brick & Blocks offers free on-site quotes across Cheltenham, Moorabbin, Hampton, and surrounding suburbs. Give us a call on +61 434 125 772 or email megabrickblocks@gmail.com to arrange your no-obligation assessment today.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Lay Block Walls in Melbourne's South-East
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the ideal seasons and weather conditions for block work in Cheltenham, and why timing matters for mortar strength and longevity.
body: Timing your block wall project in Cheltenham is more important than most homeowners realise. Melbourne's south-east experiences distinct seasonal shifts that directly affect mortar curing, concrete setting, and overall block wall quality. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we schedule our projects around these conditions to ensure every wall we build for Cheltenham clients meets Australian Standards and stands the test of time. Understanding the best time to lay block walls helps you plan your project for optimal results.

Spring and autumn are generally the best seasons for block work in Cheltenham. Temperatures between 10°C and 25°C provide ideal conditions for mortar to cure properly without drying too quickly or freezing. During these mild Melbourne shoulder seasons, moisture levels in the air also help maintain the right balance — the mortar stays workable long enough for precise placement but sets firmly within the recommended timeframe. For Cheltenham homeowners planning a new block fence or retaining wall, scheduling your project in September to November or March to May gives you the best chance of ideal conditions.

Summer block work in Melbourne's south-east requires careful management. When Cheltenham temperatures climb above 30°C — which happens regularly in January and February — mortar can dry too rapidly, leading to weak bonds and surface cracking. Professional builders like Mega Brick & Blocks mitigate this by wetting blocks before laying, shading fresh work where possible, and avoiding the hottest parts of the day. We also adjust our mortar mix to account for faster evaporation. If your Cheltenham project must happen in summer, experienced block layers know exactly how to protect the integrity of your wall.

Winter is the most challenging season for block work in Cheltenham. Melbourne's south-east can experience frost, rain, and temperatures well below 10°C from June through August. Frost is the enemy of fresh mortar — if the water in the mix freezes before curing, it expands and destroys the bond between blocks. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we avoid laying blocks during frost conditions and will postpone your Cheltenham project rather than compromise quality. Rain also dilutes mortar and can wash it out of joints before it sets, so covered or sheltered work areas are essential during wet weather.

Soil conditions in Cheltenham also influence timing. Many properties in the area sit on reactive clay that expands when wet and shrinks when dry. For retaining walls and fence footings, it is best to pour concrete footings when the soil is at a stable moisture level — typically mid-spring or mid-autumn after the extremes of summer dryness and winter saturation have passed. This ensures your footings cure on a stable base and your block wall maintains its alignment for years to come.

The bottom line for Cheltenham homeowners is this: plan ahead and book your block work with Mega Brick & Blocks early. Our busiest seasons are spring and autumn because that is when conditions are ideal — and our schedule fills quickly. By contacting us in advance, we can lock in the perfect window for your Cheltenham block fence, retaining wall, or masonry project. Call +61 434 125 772 or email megabrickblocks@gmail.com to discuss timing for your project.

blogPosts.title: Block vs Brick Fencing: Which Is Better for Cheltenham Homes?
blogPosts.excerpt: Compare block and brick fencing options for Cheltenham properties — cost, durability, aesthetics, and suitability for Melbourne's south-east.
body: Choosing between block fencing and brick fencing is one of the first decisions Cheltenham homeowners face when planning a new boundary wall. Both options offer excellent durability and security, but they differ in cost, appearance, construction method, and suitability for different site conditions. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we work with both materials daily across Cheltenham and Melbourne's south-east, so we can help you make an informed choice that suits your property, budget, and personal style.

Block fencing — typically constructed from concrete masonry units or besser blocks — is the more affordable option for most Cheltenham projects. Blocks are larger than bricks, which means fewer units to lay per square metre and faster construction times. A standard 400mm x 200mm block wall can be erected much more quickly than an equivalent brick wall, reducing labour costs significantly. For Cheltenham homeowners on a tighter budget who still want a strong, long-lasting fence, core-filled block walls offer outstanding value without compromising on structural integrity.

Brick fencing delivers a premium aesthetic that many Cheltenham homeowners prefer, particularly in heritage or period-style streetscapes. Bricks offer a wider range of colours, textures, and bond patterns, allowing for highly customised designs that complement your home's architecture. The downside is that brick fencing costs more per square metre than block due to the smaller unit size, slower laying rate, and higher material costs. For a typical Cheltenham front fence, expect to pay 30 to 50 percent more for brick compared to an equivalent block wall.

When it comes to structural performance, both block and brick fencing meet Australian Standards when constructed correctly. Core-filled block walls provide exceptional mass and wind resistance, making them ideal for Cheltenham's exposed south-eastern locations where bayside winds can be significant. Brick walls, especially double-brick construction, also offer excellent mass and durability. The key factor in both cases is proper footing design — Cheltenham's reactive clay soils demand engineered footings regardless of whether you choose block or brick.

Maintenance is another consideration for Cheltenham homeowners. Block fencing can be left raw, rendered, parged, or painted. A rendered finish is the most popular choice because it gives the wall a clean, modern appearance while protecting the blockwork from weather. Brick fencing requires less ongoing maintenance because the bricks themselves are the finished surface. However, brick mortar joints may need repointing after 20 to 30 years, whereas a well-rendered block wall can last 50 years or more with minimal upkeep.

Ultimately, the choice between block and brick fencing for your Cheltenham home comes down to budget, aesthetics, and personal preference. If cost and speed are priorities, a core-filled block wall with a rendered finish delivers outstanding value and performance. If you want the classic look of brickwork and your budget allows, brick fencing will enhance your Cheltenham property's street appeal beautifully. Mega Brick & Blocks can provide samples, advice, and a free on-site quote to help you decide. Call us on +61 434 125 772 or email megabrickblocks@gmail.com to get started.

blogPosts.title: Why Core-Filled Block Fencing Beats Timber in Cheltenham
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover why Cheltenham homeowners are switching from timber fences to core-filled block walls for superior strength, security, and longevity.
body: Timber fencing has been the default choice for Australian homes for decades, but Cheltenham homeowners are increasingly discovering that core-filled block walls offer a far superior long-term solution. At Mega Brick & Blocks, we have replaced countless failing timber fences across Cheltenham and Melbourne's south-east with robust block walls that look better, last longer, and require virtually zero maintenance. If you are weighing up your options for a new boundary fence, here is why block is the smarter investment for your Cheltenham property.

The fundamental weakness of timber fencing is its vulnerability to Melbourne's climate. Cheltenham's proximity to Port Phillip Bay means fences are exposed to moisture, salt air, UV radiation, and temperature extremes year-round. Timber absorbs moisture, swells, rots, and eventually fails — typically within 10 to 15 years. Termites are another major risk in Melbourne's south-east. Even treated timber is not immune to termite damage over time. Core-filled block walls, by contrast, are impervious to rot, termites, fire, and moisture damage. A well-constructed block fence in Cheltenham will last 50 years or more without degradation.

Security is another area where block fencing outperforms timber. A standard timber fence can be kicked in, cut, or climbed relatively easily. A two-metre high core-filled block wall is a serious physical barrier that deters intruders and provides genuine privacy for your Cheltenham home. For families with young children or pets, the solidity of a block fence gives peace of mind that timber simply cannot match. The weight and mass of a core-filled block wall also makes it extremely resistant to Melbourne's notorious wind events.

From a cost perspective, timber fencing appears cheaper upfront, but the total cost of ownership tells a different story for Cheltenham homeowners. A timber fence may cost less to install initially, but within 10 to 15 years you will likely be facing repair, staining, or complete replacement costs. A core-filled block fence from Mega Brick & Blocks has higher upfront costs but virtually zero ongoing maintenance. Over a 30-year period, block fencing often works out significantly cheaper than timber when you factor in replacement cycles, painting, staining, and repairs.

Aesthetically, block fencing offers far more versatility than timber. A raw block wall can be rendered smooth, given a textured finish, painted any colour, or combined with decorative capping and feature panels. Many Cheltenham homeowners opt for a rendered finish because it provides a clean, contemporary look that complements modern architecture. You can also integrate lighting, letterboxes, and gate openings directly into the block structure for a polished, cohesive appearance that timber fences simply cannot achieve.

If your Cheltenham timber fence is showing its age — leaning, rotting, or termite-damaged — now is the perfect time to upgrade to a core-filled block wall that will protect your property for decades.
